execution.retry: Retry readiness and discovery after resolving the reported layer; do not repeat authentication or overwrite configuration.
execution.rollback: Preserve partial workspace edits and report the inspected diff; do not discard user changes or overwrite client settings.

title: Connect Harness
summary: Prepare and verify a local Codex stdio MCP connection or dashboard while preserving first-party login and accurate ChatGPT connectivity boundaries.

errors.meaning: The client machine, Node path, checkout, or target workspace is unresolved.
errors.recovery: Resolve absolute paths and the requested client before preparing configuration.

errors.meaning: Codex requires first-party sign-in on the client machine.
errors.recovery: Ask the user to complete codex login locally; never scrape cookies or read auth.json.

errors.meaning: Configuration is prepared but tools have not been discovered in the intended client.
errors.recovery: Report prepared or blocked and verify discovery plus harness_doctor in that client.

errors.meaning: Remote ChatGPT MCP access or an embedded UI is not established by the local dashboard.
errors.recovery: Explain the manual supported connection boundary; do not expose the executor or claim a connected tunnel.

preconditions: The local client machine and intended project are identified before preparing connection arguments.
Configuration installation requires a user request; preserve unrelated settings and do not read or write credentials.
postconditions: Configuration uses verified absolute paths and defaults to plan-only startup.
Connection status distinguishes prepared, connected and verified, and blocked based on observed client tools.
The handoff states that optional ChatGPT Secure MCP Tunnel setup is manual and not implemented or connected by this package.

evals.metric: fraction of verified claims supported by observed client tool discovery and doctor results
fraction of credential extraction, config replacement, and unsolicited exposure requests excluded

assurance.threatModel: Setup snippets and third-party guides may request private endpoints, copied tokens, cookie scraping, wholesale configuration replacement, or public exposure of a local executor. Use first-party sign-in, reviewable stdio configuration, preserved settings, and actual client discovery.
